body:
Hi @mxie! Do you know if this worked on 4.2.x?

EDIT: I think the issue here is that you need to call `to_h` on `user_answer_params`, since `ActionController::Parameters` does not inherit from `Hash` in Rails 5.

@maclover7 I haven't tried it on 4.2.x, but yes, calling `to_h` does work...but you shouldn't have to though since normally, you could just pass `ActionController::Parameters` to a model and it'd save fine. It seems to be that if the parameters are nested though, they don't cast correctly.

@maclover7 Sorry, I just realized that I misread your comment, but I think I still stand by my statement that nested parameters should still work the same way as if it wasn't nested. Otherwise, it seems inconsistent.

Looked into this briefly and couldn't come up with a good solution.

``` diff
modified   activerecord/lib/active_record/connection_adapters/abstract/quoting.rb
@@ -1,4 +1,5 @@
 require "active_support/core_ext/big_decimal/conversions"
+require "action_controller/metal/strong_parameters"

 module ActiveRecord
   module ConnectionAdapters # :nodoc:
@@ -188,6 +189,7 @@ def _type_cast(value)
           when BigDecimal then value.to_s("F")
           when Type::Time::Value then quoted_time(value)
           when Date, Time then quoted_date(value)
+          when ActionController::Parameters then value.to_h
```

Seems not good because of tying AC to AR.
Also this issue is related to HStore columns only as the params hash goes upto `quoting` untouched. I haven't checked with JSON columns but this issue might be present in that case as well.

@mxie Would you be able to look into whether this worked in 4.2.x? If so, can you do a `git bisect` to determine where a possible regression was introduced? I'm curious whether this was ever supported behavior.
@maclover7 Sure! I'll take a look later this week.
Bisected, and 14a3bd520dd4bbf1247fd3e0071b59c02c115ce0 is what's introducing the error seen here.

Yes the solution is just to check for responding to `to_unsafe_h` in the
type, but I'd also like to see if we can handle this somewhere higher up.
